name: H3LIS331DL high-g 3-axis accelerometer
description: STMicroelectronics high-g 3-axis digital accelerometer, ±100/±200/±400 g selectable, 12-bit output (49 mg/digit at ±100 g), I2C/SPI, two programmable interrupt generators, data rates 0.5 Hz to 1 kHz. Chip supply 2.16–3.6 V. For impacts, crashes, rocketry and other big shocks; too coarse for tilt sensing. Sold as: Adafruit H3LIS331 Ultra High Range Triple-Axis Accelerometer breakout, STEMMA QT (#4627), modelled by its main 6-pin header VIN, 3Vo, GND, SCL, SDA, INT (3.3 V regulator, 3–5 V supply, I2C address 0x18; the second 6-pin row I2, NC, NC, NC, SDO, CS is not needed for I2C and is left unconnected: SDO open = 0x18, CS pulled high = I2C).
eli5: Measures very hard knocks and shakes on three axes, up to hundreds of times the pull of gravity.

pins.name: VIN
pins.description: Supply, 3–5 V (on-board 3.3 V regulator feeds the chip; use the same voltage as your board's logic)

pins.name: 3Vo
pins.description: 3.3 V output of the on-board regulator (up to 100 mA); not a supply input, leave unconnected

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock (10 kΩ pull-up and level shifting on the board)

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data (10 kΩ pull-up and level shifting on the board)

pins.name: INT
pins.description: Interrupt 1 output (3.3 V logic: data ready or acceleration threshold), optional

supplierQuery: Adafruit H3LIS331 high-g triple-axis accelerometer breakout 4627
buildNotes: The chip powers up in power-down mode (CTRL_REG1 0x20 = 0x07): write a power mode and data rate, e.g. 0x2F = normal mode, 100 Hz, X/Y/Z on, before reading; then wait the turn-on time 1/ODR + 1 ms.
Choose the range in CTRL_REG4 0x23 (FS bits 5:4: 00 = ±100 g, 01 = ±200 g, 11 = ±400 g); 0x80 = BDU on, ±100 g.

Read OUT_X_L..OUT_Z_H in one 6-byte burst starting at 0xA8 (0x28 with the auto-increment bit 0x80 set). Each axis is two's complement, low byte first, left-justified: shift right by 4, then 49 mg/digit at ±100 g (98 and 195 mg at ±200/±400 g).
WHO_AM_I (0x0F) must read 0x32; anything else means a wiring fault or the wrong address.
Leave the second header row unconnected for I2C at 0x18; tie SDO to 3.3 V for 0x19. Pulling CS low switches the chip to SPI.
Resolution is about 0.05 g, so at rest the readings jitter around 0 g / 1 g with an offset of up to ±1 g: this sensor is for big shocks, not tilt.
Bolt the board down firmly; the acceleration it measures only means something if the board moves with the object.

driver.code:
# H3LIS331DL high-g 3-axis accelerometer (STMicroelectronics), MicroPython driver for I2C.
# From the H3LIS331DL datasheet (DocID023111):
#   WHO_AM_I 0x0F = 0x32.
#   CTRL_REG1 0x20: PM[7:5] (000 power-down, 001 normal), DR[4:3] (00 50 Hz, 01 100 Hz,
#     10 400 Hz, 11 1000 Hz), Zen/Yen/Xen bits 2:0. Default 0x07 = power-down.
#   CTRL_REG4 0x23: BDU bit 7, BLE bit 6 (0 = LSB at lower address), FS[5:4]
#     (00 +-100 g, 01 +-200 g, 11 +-400 g).
#   STATUS_REG 0x27: ZYXDA bit 3 = new X/Y/Z set available.
#   OUT_X_L..OUT_Z_H 0x28-0x2D: two's complement, 12-bit data left-justified in 16 bits,
#     low byte first. Sensitivity 49 / 98 / 195 mg per digit (12-bit) at +-100/200/400 g.
#   I2C sub-address MSB = 1 enables auto-increment for multi-byte reads.
#   Turn-on time 1/ODR + 1 ms.
import time

_WHO_AM_I = 0x0F
_CTRL_REG1 = 0x20
_CTRL_REG4 = 0x23
_STATUS_REG = 0x27
_OUT_X_L = 0x28
_AUTO_INC = 0x80

_FS = {100: (0b00, 49), 200: (0b01, 98), 400: (0b11, 195)}  # FS bits, mg/digit


class H3LIS331DL:
    def __init__(self, i2c, addr=0x18, g_range=100):
        """addr: 0x18 with SDO/SA0 low or open (Adafruit board), 0x19 with SDO tied to 3.3 V.
        g_range: 100, 200 or 400 g full scale."""
        if g_range not in _FS:
            raise ValueError('g_range must be 100, 200 or 400')
        self.i2c = i2c
        self.addr = addr
        who = self.i2c.readfrom_mem(addr, _WHO_AM_I, 1)[0]
        if who != 0x32:
            raise OSError('H3LIS331DL not found (WHO_AM_I 0x%02X, expected 0x32): check wiring' % who)
        fs, self._mg_per_digit = _FS[g_range]
        # BDU = 1 (high/low bytes from the same sample), BLE = 0 (little endian), full scale
        self._w(_CTRL_REG4, 0x80 | (fs << 4))
        # Normal mode (PM = 001), 100 Hz (DR = 01), X/Y/Z enabled
        self._w(_CTRL_REG1, 0x2F)
        time.sleep_ms(15)  # turn-on time 1/ODR + 1 ms = 11 ms at 100 Hz

    def _w(self, reg, val):
        self.i2c.writeto_mem(self.addr, reg, bytes([val]))

    def data_ready(self):
        """True when STATUS_REG ZYXDA says a new X/Y/Z set is available."""
        return bool(self.i2c.readfrom_mem(self.addr, _STATUS_REG, 1)[0] & 0x08)

    def raw(self):
        """(x, y, z) 12-bit counts, from one 6-byte auto-increment burst at OUT_X_L."""
        for _ in range(25):  # wait up to ~25 ms (over two samples at 100 Hz) for fresh data
            if self.data_ready():
                break
            time.sleep_ms(1)
        d = self.i2c.readfrom_mem(self.addr, _OUT_X_L | _AUTO_INC, 6)
        out = []
        for i in (0, 2, 4):
            v = d[i] | (d[i + 1] << 8)  # OUT_x_L = low byte, OUT_x_H = high byte
            if v & 0x8000:
                v -= 65536
            out.append(v >> 4)  # 12-bit value is left-justified in bits 15:4
        return tuple(out)

    def read(self):
        """(x, y, z) acceleration in g."""
        k = self._mg_per_digit / 1000
        x, y, z = self.raw()
        return x * k, y * k, z * k

    def read_ms2(self):
        """(x, y, z) acceleration in m/s^2."""
        return tuple(v * 9.80665 for v in self.read())

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from h3lis331dl import H3LIS331DL

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
accel = H3LIS331DL(i2c)  # +-100 g range
while True:
    x, y, z = accel.read()
    print('X=%.1f Y=%.1f Z=%.1f g' % (x, y, z))
    time.sleep(1)
